run: FMB1 run 44 (replay_20261023_083639, 687 s, 411 s still in intervals >= 0.8 s) + its reset (08:25:06-08:36:38, 692 s: disassemble x4 543 s, move_base ~142 s)
caveats: arm_still_seconds = TCP translation still (motion recorder). A wrist turn in place counts as still.

seconds_per_run sums over the run (per cycle for 'reset:' rows). Values marked estimate in 'why' are not timed (drive_align had no read_icp/turn_wrist rows before 255d950; move_base has no timing file).
needed='partly' means the output is used but the same output is available cheaper; 'unclear' means the effect on seating was not measured.

entries.produces: arm at home, camera over the home-visible table
entries.why: Start pose for the up-front planning observe (it saw u_orange there: 'derive-sequence u_orange: observed rpy... 1 pass').

entries.produces: fingers fully open (move_base left them closed at 0.5 mm)
entries.why: Needed after move_base (fingers closed for pushing). But move_to_grasp then commands the pre-grasp width (35 mm) before the descent, a second gripper call (2.4 s, log 'Restoring gripper to initial width (35mm)').
entries.cheaper_alternative: Open to the first part's pre-grasp opening only if the views do not need a fully open hand; otherwise keep. Small (~2.4 s).

entries.produces: pass count per part seen from home (u_orange) + LAST_SEEN_XY
entries.why: Arm passes home anyway; one shared still window (CLAUDE.md: plan every part up front).

entries.action: view the clear area (+1.5 s sleep + observe_many)
entries.produces: u_brown pass count (rpy -90,0,21.6 -> 1 pass) + LAST_SEEN_XY
entries.why: u_brown is picked first, from the clear area: the depth-pick view above it 1 min later (0.52 m, same part) could plan it. The only reason to plan up front is a part the per-part view cannot see, and every part now gets a straight-down view before its pick (_part_view / depth-pick view).
entries.cheaper_alternative: Plan u_brown at its depth-pick view (derive_sequence_for with the depth-pick samples), drop this view.

entries.produces: line_green pass count; inverted_u_yellow NOT seen ('not seen from any view -> recorded sequence') -> _planned_blind
entries.why: 11.4 s move (0.78 m Cartesian, commanded 10 s) for one part's pass count; the yellow is not seen from it (also unseen in all 3 reset landing checks: spacing 'unseen': ['inverted_u_yellow']) and gets re-planned at its own view anyway. line_green gets its own 'view above line_green' 3 min later.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Plan each part at its own view above it (as the yellow already is), or from the disassembly's recorded set-down pose (record_staged keeps the stance; staged_parts.json is loaded at 4113). Saves ~16 s.

entries.produces: camera 0.56 m over the last base read
entries.why: The one empty-gripper whole-base view of the run (BASE_FROM=icp needs the base beyond the D415 0.45 m depth floor).

entries.produces: marker base pose (15 samples)
entries.why: With BASE_FROM=icp the markers only seed the CAD fit. seams/vision_ops.py:pose 77-93 already seeds from last_base_pose.json for this reason ('A certify spent 15.2 s here (10-23): markers 5.5 + a depth outline only a refused fallback used 3.3 + the fit 4.3'). Here the last read is move_base's final read, 2 min old.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Seed read_icp from _last_base_pose (move_base's final read); markers only if that fit fails. ~5 s.

entries.produces: outline base pose (fallback only)
entries.why: _choose_base_read 975-991: with BASE_FROM=icp the outline is returned only when the ICP fit fails; run 44's fit succeeded (rms 1.17 mm), so the 4.6 s gap before base_read bought nothing. The 1 s sleep is also redundant: capture() waits for frames >= 1.2 s after the TCP stopped (handeye_icp_survey.py:capture 73-79).
entries.cheaper_alternative: Compute the outline lazily, only when read_icp returns None.

entries.produces: args.observed_base + last_base_pose.json (base1 at 145.9,-485.3 mm, 19.23 deg)
consumed_by: drive --mate (measured base for mate:00 -> track_base_in_hand view position / seed)
execute_mate: certify base fit (seed via last_base_pose.json)
entries.why: The base pose every first aim starts from; the in-hand read then moved it 5.1 mm (drive_align_u_brown log).

entries.produces: arm over the clear area; u_brown confirmed there (brightness + observe)
entries.why: The depth-pick view above u_brown follows straight after (5.0 s move from 0.32 m back up to 0.52 m) and fits the part there; that view would also say 'not here'.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Return straight to the depth-pick view above u_brown (one move, no _seen_here). ~6 s.

entries.produces: wrist_3 within its cable range ('unwound_turns': 0)
entries.why: Cable safety (memory: wrist_3 wind-up). 1 s is mostly process start.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Check wrist_3 from the state tap in process; call the primitive only when it is wound.

entries.produces: arm at home ('camera view of the table')
entries.why: Nothing reads the home view: with --part-at-staging and u_orange last seen away from the clear area the next step is _part_view (4370), which flies above u_orange. line_green/yellow already skip it (NOT_FROM_HOME).
entries.cheaper_alternative: Skip move_home when the next step is _part_view (same condition as 4365-4370).

entries.action: part view: view above <part> at 0.52 m (+1.5 s sleep, brightness, _seen_here observe)
entries.produces: part confirmed under the camera; LAST_SEEN_XY / tracker xy (moves the target 6-12 mm)
entries.why: The view itself is needed (the part is out of view from where the last insert left the arm). But it is the SAME pose as the depth-pick view (0.52 m top-down over the part) except for the 6-12 mm the observe moved LAST_SEEN_XY, and its samples are thrown away: part_depth.read observes again 1-2 s later.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Make the part view the depth-pick view: keep its samples as the fit seed; widen depth_pick_target's 'already there' test (2579: 5 mm) to the fit's crop (CROP_R_M 0.11 m).

entries.action: yellow planned-blind re-plan (_seen_here x2 + derive observe)
entries.produces: inverted_u_yellow tool_sequence (1 pass, RESHAPED)
entries.why: _part_view returned True only after _seen_here saw it (852); then 4421 _seen_here(4 s), 4423 _seen_here(8 s) and derive_sequence_for's own observe ran again from the same still pose: 3 brightness + 4 observes in 7 s (timing +330.5..337.5). Root cause: the reset puts the yellow where the staging view never detects it.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Pass the _part_view samples to derive_sequence_for(samples=...); skip both extra _seen_here calls. ~6 s.

entries.produces: camera straight above the part at depth height
entries.why: u_brown: needed (arm was at 0.32 m over the clear area). u_orange and yellow: re-centring moves of 7.9 mm / 12.1 mm ('distance_m': 0.0079 / 0.0121) taking 3.9 / 3.8 s because the 'already there' test is 5 mm; line_green (within 5 mm) skipped it.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Skip the re-centre when within the fit crop (0.11 m); for u_brown come straight here from the base view. ~8-12 s.

entries.produces: marker pose of the part (8 still samples) to seed the CAD fit
entries.why: The part view observed the same part from the same pose 1-5 s earlier (_seen_here) and the startup observes produced samples too; this is a third/fourth marker read. Not separately timed: inside the 7.5-9.3 s still gap before each move_to_grasp.
entries.cheaper_alternative: part_depth.read(part, seed=<samples from the view>) - the seed parameter already exists (83).

entries.produces: grasp point xyz + object quat from the depth fit (moved 1.3-3.3 mm from the marker seed)
entries.why: Operator rule 10-21: picks from depth (finger landed on line_green from a 9-10 mm marker error). The 32.8 s is the whole still gap incl. the seed observe above; the capture alone waits for frames >= 1.2 s after the stop.

entries.where: primitives/move_to_grasp.py (step 1 hover, step 2 fine positioning; step 3 skipped with --target-xyz)
entries.produces: part between the open fingers at the grasp; current_object_orientation (chained)
entries.why: The pick itself. Its still time includes the two gripper subprocesses below and ~1 s process start.

entries.produces: fingers at 100 mm for a camera view
entries.why: With --target-xyz from the depth fit move_to_grasp never looks ('Skipping step 3 (explicit --target-xyz from the depth fit)'). FIXED after run 44 by 0a9229f.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Done (0a9229f).

entries.action: control_gripper pre-grasp width (inside move_to_grasp, before the descent)
entries.where: primitives/move_to_grasp.py step 2 ('Restoring gripper to initial width')
entries.produces: fingers at the pre-grasp opening
entries.why: Needed for u_brown (100 mm after the startup open). For u_orange/line_green/yellow it only undid the open-for-view above. The trajectory waits for it (log: control_gripper 882.66 -> 885.08, then 'Step 2 trajectory sent'). 0a9229f now skips it when the fingers are within 3 mm.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Done for 3 of 4 parts (0a9229f). For the first part: open to the pre-grasp width at startup, or send it during step 1's hover move.

entries.produces: part gripped; final_width_mm
entries.why: The grasp. ~1 s of each 1.7 s is process start.

entries.produces: part lifted to 0.32 m flange
entries.why: CLAUDE.md: reorient at safe height.

entries.produces: part at its target orientation relative to an IDENTITY base yaw; final_object_orientation (snapped fold branch)
entries.why: The reorient is needed (its snapped quaternion is what the insert chain was validated with - replay 3523-3532). But in real mode it ignores the measured base yaw (rotate_object.py:1188-1192 'Real mode: always use default [0, 0, 0, 1]'), so every part arrives ~19-20 deg off the base and drive_align turns the wrist (+19.79, +20.26, +19.08, +18.75 deg in run 44). The verify_grasp inside (~1.2 s, width only) repeats the close's own width check.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Pass the measured base yaw into rotate_object (primitive outside compliant_insertion_studio - ask the operator) so the base-yaw turn disappears; --skip-verify-grasp exists (rotate_object.py:1881).

entries.produces: nothing (PRE_INSERT_READ=off)
entries.why: Disabled in this recipe; the in-hand read inside drive-mate replaces it.

entries.action: drive --mate seam overhead (client + server + drive_align / translate_object / touch_insert process starts)
entries.produces: plumbing
entries.why: Per part: ~1.6 s before the first align row (depth route; the marker route's 5.6 s includes a wrist turn), ~3.5-4.7 s between the align child's last row and 'aligned' in /tmp/drive_mate.log (drive_align imports the 4600-line replay module, 0.5 s poll), then translate_object spawns touch_insert (two more process starts). Estimate from row offsets.
entries.cheaper_alternative: One long-lived drive-mate worker that has the replay/align code imported (AR3 debt noted in seams/drive_align.py docstring); call touch_insert directly.

entries.produces: held part turned to the measured base yaw (held_q updated)
entries.why: Needed only because rotate_object targets an identity base yaw (see above). Each turn is a move_cartesian SUBPROCESS (~1.5 s start + 2.5 s min duration). A pure wrist turn does not translate the TCP, so the motion recorder counts it as still. Estimate 4 x ~4 s (gaps of 4.1-4.3 s around turns in the drive_align timing).
entries.cheaper_alternative: Fold the yaw into rotate_object's target, or into the next in-process move (_move_unless_there to the base track view can carry the turned quaternion).

entries.produces: wrist turned by the image yaw; another measuring round
entries.why: u_brown -1.55 and -0.47 deg, u_orange -1.93, yellow -0.41 deg. SERVO_YAW_MIN_TURN_DEG = 0.4 is the stated noise floor (seams/servo_law.py:26); the -0.47/-0.41 turns cleared it by <0.1 deg and each cost a turn (~4 s) + a re-measure round (u_brown: up 2.7 + hover 3.0 + frame 1.3 s). Whether such turns change the seat is not measured.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Do the turn in process (no subprocess); test a 0.6-0.8 deg threshold against the seat outcome before changing it.

entries.action: base track view (part in hand) - marker route
entries.produces: camera 0.56 m over the base with the part in hand
entries.why: The marker servo then measures part vs socket against the base's own markers IN THE SAME FRAME every round (base_pose_same_frame), and the aim returned is the servoed xy (aim = base + total servo move), so the in-hand read mostly sets the starting guess, rim heights and drive-mate's measured base. It did move the base 5.1 / 2.8 mm (u_brown / u_orange) since the startup read.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Not tested: start the servo from the previous measured base and keep the same-frame base read; compare rounds and seat error over a few runs before dropping it.

entries.produces: base pose fitted to depth with the seated parts (drive-mate's measured base)
consumed_by: drive --mate result base_measured -> next part's start base
entries.why: Each read = still_frame for the marker seed (~1.0 s) + depth capture (>= 1.2 s after stop) + fit; the 6.2-8.8 s still gaps after the base-track rows include it. For line_green it FAILED both times ('CAD fit failed in hand ... partial view' / 'tilted fit') - and in 31 of 34 line_green reads in today's drive_align logs - so it fell back to 'aiming at the previous read'. Estimate ~3.5 s per read x 6.
entries.cheaper_alternative: line_green: skip the in-hand base read (it fails by construction with the U parts seated; held_axial_correction from the outline is what it actually uses).

entries.action: base track view #1 (depth route, before the outline)
entries.produces: first in-hand base read (line_green: failed; yellow: ok)
consumed_by: depth_servo wrist turn to base yaw (only)
entries.why: depth_servo re-reads the base itself after the outline view (1939). Yellow's second read moved only 0.7 mm / +0.56 deg from the first; line_green's both failed. The same redundancy was already removed for the marker route (2094-2097 'a read here first, before the turn, only fed that turn (run 34: ~15 s per U part)'). Move 7.65 / 6.09 s + frame 1.1 s + fit.
entries.cheaper_alternative: For the depth route turn the wrist from the measured base and go straight to the outline view (as the marker route does). ~10-12 s per depth-route part.

entries.action: servo/dservo: outline view over table (+ still_frame + held_outline_px)
entries.produces: held part's outline in the image over bare table (camera rigid with the gripper)
entries.why: The only read of where the part sits in the hand; line_green's insert aim came from it.

entries.action: _emitter toggles (D415 projector on/off via ros2 param CLI)
entries.produces: projector state (colour frames without the dot pattern)
consumed_by: read_icp / certify depth capture (projector back on)
entries.why: Each set is a `ros2 param set` process + 0.8 s sleep (~2.2 s; 2.2-2.4 s gaps around the dservo outline still_frame: line_green +24.3->26.7 and +27.6->29.8 s). Marker route: 2 sets per part; depth route: 4 (off/on around the outline frame, off again for the rounds, on at release). The reason is a DARK room (docstring 10-21); run 44 ran with the lights on.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Set the parameter in process (rclpy param client, no CLI start); skip when ensure_exposure's brightness is normal; in depth_servo read the base first, then outline + rounds in one off-window (2 sets instead of 4). Estimate 12 x 2.2 s.

entries.action: servo rounds (clear / hover / still_frame / base_pose_same_frame / socket_shift_world)
entries.produces: aim correction (u_brown -4.1,-7.7 mm; u_orange -1.9,-0.4 mm; yellow converged -3.0/+0.1 mm)
entries.why: u_brown round 0 read 8.6 mm off - the grasp error the insert cannot absorb blind. Estimate from the drive_align rows.

entries.produces: arm at the clear height over the aim
entries.why: touch_insert's first move is to its own hover at the same xy (drive_mate log 'FK current [0.1825,-0.5252,0.2880] -> Target [0.1823,-0.5253,0.2880]'), so this move is the hover; fine, but u_orange's servo 'clear 1' then 'done' moved to the same place twice.

entries.produces: seated part; slide / measured_correction; insert CSV/meta
entries.why: 13.6 / 13.6 / 38.7 / 16.1 s. line_green needed 9 probes (8 stopped +34 mm on the U tops) because its aim came from the outline only (in-hand base fit failed).

entries.produces: part released at rest
entries.why: A free mate is judged after release (execute_mate_server premise 4).

entries.produces: fingers lifted clear of the seated part
entries.why: Straight up out of the seated part (CLAUDE.md safe height rule).

entries.produces: depth seat verdict (pitch -0.84, height +0.79 mm) + seat error [-0.9, 0.0] mm + a re-fitted base
entries.why: ExecuteMate measures the same seat with the same depth seat check (seams/vision_ops.py:certify_many 236) from the same 'outer' view seconds later (the seat view move was 2.1 mm). The non-one-node branch (3916-3926) already runs the ladder only on a measured not_at_seat.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Certify first; run the seat-check ladder only on not_at_seat; take the yellow's follow error from the certify's depth result. ~13 s.

entries.produces: camera at the side view that measured this mate last time
entries.why: The seat height is only measurable from a side view. line_green's 2.1 mm move still took 3.9 s (2.5 s min duration + process start).
entries.cheaper_alternative: Skip moves under ~3 mm (as _move_unless_there does for servo moves).

entries.produces: base pose for the seat measurement
consumed_by: execute_mate: depth capture + measure (seat height vs CAD)
entries.why: 4.3-5.5 s per certify ([certify timing] base_pose). From the mate:01 and mate:02 views the fit FAILS ('fit -3.1 / +3.5 mm off the table height') and the certify uses the last saved read anyway - those ~10 s produce nothing. It also takes its own depth capture, then capture_world takes a second one from the same still pose.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Fit the base on the capture_world frames (one capture); or seed/accept drive-mate's measured base when the fit is refused from this view. ~11-20 s.

entries.action: execute_mate: depth capture + per-mate measure (+ marker xy read)
entries.produces: seat height/tilt of this mate and every predecessor; placed / refusal
entries.why: The certification the operator asked for after every seat (memory per-seat-check). Predecessor re-reads are 0.5 s each (contract: 'every predecessor still passes NOW').

entries.produces: colour-frame brightness (exposure guard)
entries.why: One camera process per call (~1 s), 9 calls. FIXED after run 44 by 255d950 (a normal reading under 60 s old is reused).

entries.where: ablations/replay_real_assembly.py:replay_object 3886 'Tiny pause between primitives to let TF + topics settle'
entries.produces: nothing measurable
entries.why: Every primitive is a subprocess that already waited for its own completion; reads that need stillness use the still-window rule (observe_many settle(), still_frame, capture). 28 x 0.5 s gaps in the timing (e.g. 888.01 -> 888.53).
entries.cheaper_alternative: Remove, or keep only before a read that does not apply the still rule.

entries.action: fixed settle sleeps before still-window reads
entries.produces: time
entries.why: observe_many/_OBSERVE_*_HELPER and capture() already accept only samples taken after the TCP was still (memory depth-timing: 'stamp rule >=0.25 s after still replaces sleeps'). 1.5 s gaps before observe_many in the timing (+15.8, +31.7 s).
entries.cheaper_alternative: Drop the sleeps; rely on the still-window rule.

entries.produces: flange moved DOWN from 0.4716 to 0.2986 m
entries.why: The arm is at the last certify seat view, 0.47 m up, gripper empty ('FK current: [0.0428, -0.2487, 0.4716]', target flange Z 0.2986). The safe-height rule is for a gripped part in the base.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Skip when the gripper is empty and the flange is already above SAFE_HEIGHT.

entries.produces: arm at home (end state)
entries.why: The next disassembly starts with its own move_home (disassemble.py:828), which then takes 4.0 s for a zero-distance move.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Keep one of the two.

entries.action: reset: home (start of each disassemble process)
entries.produces: arm at home
entries.why: The next move is the base view (observe_base 394). The first call followed run 43's cleanup move_home (already home); the other three follow the previous process's staging-view landing check.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Go straight to the base view; or run all four parts in ONE disassemble process (no per-process start/end).

entries.action: reset: open (start of each disassemble process)
entries.produces: fingers fully open
entries.why: The seat grasp sets 'open to release width' before the descent anyway (1063); the open only keeps the fingers out of the base view. After the previous part's release the fingers are already at w+6 mm.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Skip when the fingers are already open wider than the part (one gripper read).

entries.produces: camera 0.56 m over the base
entries.why: Needed once per part for the seat grasp; the second per --to-free-spot part only re-reads an untouched base (see below).

entries.produces: marker base pose (seed)
entries.why: 6.1-6.8 s each; with BASE_FROM=icp only a seed. vision_ops already seeds from the last saved read instead.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Seed read_icp from _last_base_pose (seconds old within a reset); markers only when that fit fails. ~40 s per reset.

entries.produces: outline base pose (fallback only)
entries.why: Every reset read's ICP succeeded (rms 1.17-1.21 mm); the 4.1-4.6 s gap before each base_read row was spent on an unused fallback.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Compute only when read_icp fails. ~30 s per reset.

entries.produces: base pose for the seat grasp + obstacle for the free-spot choice + last_base_pose.json
consumed_by: reset: hover above the seated grasp (seat_grasp)
entries.why: One read per part is the seat-grasp reference (the pull-out can creep the base/slider - disassemble.py 987-991).

entries.action: reset: second base read per part (back over the base after the staging view)
entries.produces: the same base pose again (moved 0.3-3.9 mm vs the read ~50 s earlier)
consumed_by: reset: hover above the seated grasp
entries.why: Between the read at 936/993 and this one the arm only went to the staging view and back - nothing touched the base. Base view move + markers + outline + ICP = 20.1-21.2 s each (observe_base rows at +54.3, +55.5, +56.9 s). The reported shifts (e.g. 148.1 -> 148.3 mm, yaw 19.90 -> 20.22) are read scatter, not motion.
entries.cheaper_alternative: From the staging view go straight to 'hover above the seated grasp' with the first read (the hover's own seat read corrects the grasp anyway). ~60 s per reset.

entries.produces: wrist_3 in range
entries.why: Cable safety; mostly process start.
entries.cheaper_alternative: In-process check from the state tap.

entries.action: reset: staging view (choose a free spot) + 1.5 s sleep + observe_parts
entries.produces: poses of the parts already in the staging region (obstacles)
entries.why: The previous process ended ~25 s earlier with 'staging view (check the landings)' + observe of the same, unchanged scene (only the base view happened in between). The yellow is never seen from here (kept as an obstacle from staged_parts.json).
entries.cheaper_alternative: Reuse the landing check's observation (write it to staged_parts.json with poses) when nothing was set down since; or run all parts in one process. ~45 s per reset.

entries.produces: flange target (x, y) for the set-down + gap
entries.why: A 10 mm grid over the staging region, polygon gaps to every obstacle and finger outline per cell, in Python on the i5-8500T: 12.7-15.6 s of still gap after each observe_parts. Its result is consumed only by 'carry to spot', ~45-55 s later (after base view, hover, descend, close, pull-out).
entries.cheaper_alternative: Compute it in a thread while the arm does the seat grasp; and/or coarse-to-fine grid / vectorised gaps. ~40 s per reset.

entries.action: reset: hover above the seated grasp + 1 s sleep + seat read (observe part)
entries.produces: the seated part's own pose (seen -3.2..-5.7 mm, +7.4 mm from its CAD seat)
consumed_by: reset: descend onto the seated grasp
entries.why: Grasping a seated part 3-7 mm off its CAD seat needs the measurement. The 1 s sleep is redundant with the still-window rule.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Drop the sleep.

entries.produces: fingers at the release width
consumed_by: reset: descend onto the seated grasp
entries.why: Fingers must fit between seated parts.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Could be issued during the hover move (async) instead of after it.

entries.action: reset: descend onto the seated grasp (min-duration 6 s, 5 N guard)
entries.produces: fingers around the seated part
entries.why: Guarded descent into the assembly.

entries.produces: part gripped

entries.action: reset: verify_grasp x2 (after close, after pull-out)
entries.produces: width-only 'still held' verdict
entries.why: The one after the pull-out catches a part that came out of the jaws (2026-10-15 incident). The one right after close repeats what the close's own result (final_width_mm) already says. Each is a process (~1.5 s).
entries.cheaper_alternative: Check the close result's width in process; keep the post-pull-out check (in process, from /gripper_width). ~6-10 s.

entries.action: reset: pull out to safe height
entries.produces: part lifted out of the base
part over its set-down spot

entries.action: reset: lower to 15 mm above the touch + land (slow, until 5 N)
entries.produces: part resting on the table (touchdown at |dF| 5 N)
entries.why: Operator's 5 N limit on parts; slow last 15 mm so it does not bounce/tip (move_down alone landed at 17-44 N, place_at docstring).

entries.produces: part set down, gripper clear; staged_parts.json record
arm at home
entries.why: Immediately followed by the staging-view move; the next process then starts with another home.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Lift straight to the staging view.

entries.action: reset: staging view (check the landings) + brightness + observe_parts
entries.produces: spacing verdict ([spacing] ok) - parts seen in the staging region
entries.why: A real guard (a tipped/slid part), but its observation is discarded and the next process re-observes the unchanged scene ~25 s later; the yellow is 'unseen' in all three checks, so it never checked the yellow.
entries.cheaper_alternative: One landing check after the LAST set-down (single process), and feed its poses to the next spot choice and to the replay's planning (staged_parts.json with poses).

entries.action: reset: move_base initial reads (read at the clear area -> view -> read -> view -> read)
entries.produces: base pose before the pushes
entries.why: u_brown's --to-staging left the arm over the clear area; read_base there failed ('markers not read -> depth CAD fit from the last pose: only 368 points'), then view + read, then view(ob) + 1.5 s + read AGAIN at the same pose (176). Not timed; estimate from subprocess minimums.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Check the TCP against _last_base_pose first and fly to it (no blind read); drop the second view+read at 176. ~15 s.

entries.action: reset: move_base push (close, safe height, over start, lower beside the face, push, back off, lift)
entries.produces: base slid/turned toward the layout pose
entries.why: The layout pose is a reset target, not an assembly need: the assembly measures the base (startup read, in-hand reads, servo). Tolerance 5 mm / 1 deg makes it run every cycle (base drifts +8-11 mm / +2 deg per assembly: runs 42/43/44 started at -10.6, -7.8, -8.8 mm). Pushes are systematically short: in runs 42/43 the 5-7 mm turn pushes moved the base 0.2-1.3 mm each until the 'did not move it -> 4 mm further' boost (move_base.py 216-219) - 4 pushes per cycle. Total move_base 142 s in run 44 (2 pushes), ~4 min in runs 42/43.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Widen the tolerance to what the assembly region/view actually needs (e.g. only when the base nears the region edge); start pushes with the measured ~4 mm shortfall; keep the boost across cycles. Saves most of 2-4 min per cycle.

entries.produces: base pose after the push
entries.why: Needed to close the loop, but the markers (up to 8 s) only seed the ICP; the pre-push pose + the push displacement is a better seed. Estimate.
entries.cheaper_alternative: Seed read_icp from the previous read shifted by the commanded push; no markers, no 1.5 s sleep.
